proposals.before: His grandfather Senglang had been Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat in the Song, with commissioner rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
proposals.after: His grandfather Senglang had been Left Glorious Grand Master in the Song, with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
proposals.reason: 左光祿 is Left Glorious Grand Master, not Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

proposals.before: His grandfather Senglang served in Song as Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies.
proposals.after: His grandfather Senglang served in Song as Left Glorious Grand Master with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 左光祿 as secretariat director.

proposals.before: Huan had been given in adoption to succeed his father's cousin Qiu, Secretariat Director, and therefore took the style name Yansun.
proposals.after: Huan had been given in adoption to succeed his paternal granduncle Qiu, Secretariat Director, and therefore took the style name Yansun.
proposals.reason: 從祖 is a grandfather-generation paternal relative, not father's cousin.

proposals.before: Huan was adopted out to succeed his father's cousin, the Secretariat Director Qiu; hence his style name Yansun.
proposals.after: Huan was adopted out to succeed his paternal granduncle, the Secretariat Director Qiu; hence his style name Yansun.
proposals.reason: Same kinship error for 從祖.

proposals.before: He was recalled to serve as Minister of the Imperial Clan and then put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel.
proposals.after: He was recalled to serve as Minister of the Bureau of Sacrifices and then put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel.
proposals.reason: 祠部尚書 is the sacrificial bureau, not the Imperial Clan (宗正).

proposals.before: He was summoned as Minister of the Imperial Clan and then transferred to head the Ministry of Personnel.
proposals.after: He was summoned as Minister of the Bureau of Sacrifices and then transferred to head the Ministry of Personnel.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 祠部尚書.

proposals.before: Huan was therefore made Left Vice Director with the added post of Attendant Within the Gates, then sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Jing Province, and Suixiang in Si Province, General Who Guards the North, and Governor of Yong Province.
proposals.after: Huan was therefore made Left Vice Director with the added post of Attendant Within the Gates, then sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Ying Province, and Sui Commandery in Si Province, General Who Guards the North, and Governor of Yong Province.
proposals.reason: 郢州 is Ying Province, not Jing (荊州); 竟陵 belongs to Ying, and 隨郡 is Sui Commandery rather than Suixiang.

proposals.before: He was therefore transferred to Left Vice Director, with the added post of Attendant Within the Gates, and sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Jing Province, and Suixiang in Si Province, General Who Guards the North, and Governor of Yong Province.
proposals.after: He was therefore transferred to Left Vice Director, with the added post of Attendant Within the Gates, and sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Ying Province, and Sui Commandery in Si Province, General Who Guards the North, and Governor of Yong Province.
proposals.reason: 郢州 is Ying Province, not Jing Province; 隨郡 is Sui Commandery.

proposals.before: Huan's eldest son Rong, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, and Rong's younger brother Chen, Attendant in the Secretariat, were executed in the market at the capital.
proposals.after: Huan's eldest son Rong, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, and Rong's younger brother Chen, Attendant Gentleman of the Minister of Works, were executed in the market at the capital.
proposals.reason: 司徒從事中郎 is an attendant gentleman on the staff of the Minister of Works (司徒), not an office of the Secretariat.

proposals.before: Rui, still in the womb, was also marked for execution; his great-grandfather by marriage Wang Senglang petitioned Emperor Xiaowu on his behalf, and he was spared.
proposals.after: Rui, still in the womb, was also marked for execution; his maternal great-grandfather Wang Senglang petitioned Emperor Xiaowu on his behalf, and he was spared.
proposals.reason: 外曾祖 is the mother's grandfather (maternal great-grandfather), not a great-grandfather by marriage.

proposals.before: Rui, still in the womb, was also to be put to death with the clan; his great-grandfather by marriage Wang Senglang petitioned Emperor Xiaowu to save him, and he was spared.
proposals.after: Rui, still in the womb, was also to be put to death with the clan; his maternal great-grandfather Wang Senglang petitioned Emperor Xiaowu to save him, and he was spared.
proposals.reason: 外曾祖 is the mother's grandfather (maternal great-grandfather), not a great-grandfather by marriage.

proposals.before: The daughter of Huan's younger sister was consort to Prince Huang of Changsha. Emperor Shizu decreed, "Huan brought treason upon himself, but the Princess of Changsha's children are grown, and Huan himself was given in adoption—precedents exist from earlier ages; their ties shall not be severed."
proposals.after: The daughter of Huan's younger brother was consort to Prince Huang of Changsha. Emperor Shizu decreed, "Huan brought treason upon himself, but the Princess of Changsha's children are grown, and Huan himself was given in adoption—precedents exist from earlier ages; their ties shall not be severed."
proposals.reason: 奐弟女 is the daughter of Huan's younger brother (niece), not the daughter of a younger sister.

proposals.before: Huan's younger sister's daughter was consort to Prince Huang of Changsha. Emperor Shizu's edict said: "Huan brought himself into treason; the Princess of Changsha's sons and daughters are both grown, and moreover Huan was given in adoption—former ages perhaps had precedents; they may specially not be severed."
proposals.after: Huan's younger brother's daughter was consort to Prince Huang of Changsha. Emperor Shizu's edict said: "Huan brought himself into treason; the Princess of Changsha's sons and daughters are both grown, and moreover Huan was given in adoption—former ages perhaps had precedents; they may specially not be severed."
proposals.reason: 奐弟女 is the daughter of Huan's younger brother, not of a younger sister.

proposals.before: When Shizu was General Who Pacifies the Army, Minister of Personnel Zhang Dai selected Hui as his chief administrator and presented the nomination.
proposals.after: When Shizu was General Who Consoles the Army, Minister of Personnel Zhang Dai selected Hui as his chief administrator and presented the nomination.
proposals.reason: 撫軍 is General Who Consoles/Comforts the Army, not the Pacifying (寧朔) title.

proposals.before: Emperor Shizu sent Crown Prince Wen Hui to accompany the prince to Hui's house for a feast with music; dukes and ministers all came in full court dress—the age regarded it as the highest honor.
proposals.after: Emperor Shizu sent Crown Prince Wenhui to accompany the prince to Hui's house for a feast with music; dukes and ministers all came in full court dress—the age regarded it as the highest honor.
proposals.reason: 文惠太子 is the crown prince's posthumous title Wenhui, not a given name Wen Hui, which collides with Wang Hui in the same sentence.

proposals.before: Chong had been given in adoption to succeed his father's elder cousin Jingyin, Attendant Within; his childhood name was Cha, and his father Shao's childhood name was Li.
proposals.after: Chong had been given in adoption to succeed his father's elder cousin Jingyin, Attendant Within; Chong's childhood name was Cha, and Jingyin's father Shao had the childhood name Li.
proposals.reason: 父邵，小名梨 names Jingyin's father Shao (childhood name Li), not Chong's father, already introduced as Jian. The Emperor Wen joke compares Cha (Chong) with Li (Shao).

proposals.before: He was offered a post as aide in the Southern Palace of the General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Marshal but declined.
proposals.after: He was offered a post as aide to the Southern Central Commander under the General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Marshal but declined.
proposals.reason: 南中郎 is the Southern Central Commander office, not a Southern Palace.

proposals.before: Yuansi was granted provisional staff of authority under the title Ziyang.
proposals.after: Yuansi and Ziyang were granted provisional staffs of authority.
proposals.reason: 假元嗣子陽節 names Yuansi and Ziyang as two recipients of the staff of authority, not a title Ziyang conferred on Yuansi alone.

proposals.before: Yuansi was given provisional staff of authority as Ziyang.
proposals.after: Yuansi and Ziyang were given provisional staffs of authority.
proposals.reason: The Chinese coordinates 元嗣 and 子陽 as the persons granted the jie, matching Wu Ziyang named in the previous relief column.

proposals.before: Donghun appointed Cheng Mao commander of Ying and Si provinces, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Ying Province, and Yuansi commander of Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Jing Province, and Suixiang in Si Province, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Yong Province—both with staffs of authority.
proposals.after: Donghun appointed Cheng Mao commander of Ying and Si provinces, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Ying Province, and Yuansi commander of Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Ying Province, and Sui Commandery in Si Province, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Yong Province—both with staffs of authority.
proposals.reason: Chinese 郢州之竟陵 is Jingling of Ying Province (郢州), not Jing Province; 隨郡 is Sui Commandery, not the place-name Suixiang.

proposals.before: His awakening came too late; clear judgment had just been extended.
proposals.after: His awakening came too late; clear judgment was still far off.
proposals.reason: 賒 means distant or far, so 辯見方賒 is that discernment was still remote, not that it had just been extended.

decisions.reason: 宋左光祿 is Left Glorious Grand Master (左光祿大夫), not Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat (尚書左僕射); 儀同 is ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, so the replacement is accurate.
The literal field repeats the same office error: 左光祿 is Left Glorious Grand Master, not secretariat director.
從祖 names a paternal relative of the grandfather generation (paternal granduncle), not a father's cousin (從父/從伯); 出繼從祖中書令球 requires that correction.
The literal likewise misreads 從祖 as father's cousin; paternal granduncle matches the kinship term.
祠部尚書 is minister of the sacrificial bureau, not the Imperial Clan office (宗正); the replacement restores the bureau named in the source.
The literal repeats the 祠部尚書 error; Minister of the Bureau of Sacrifices is the correct office.
郢州之竟陵 is Jingling in Ying Province, not Jing Province (荊州), and 司州之隨郡 is Sui Commandery in Si Province, not Suixiang.
